members.title: China’s proposed economic corridor: What it means for Bangladesh
members.lead: China has proposed an economic corridor linking Kunming, the capital of its southwestern Yunnan province, with Bangladesh via Myanmar's coastal port of Kyaukphyu. Under the proposed arrangement, goods would travel overland from Kunming to Kyaukphyu and then by sea to Bangladesh. Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed the corridor connecting China, Myanmar and Bangladesh during a meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in Beijing on 26 June. The proposal was mentioned in an official statement issued by China's foreign ministry after the meeting. However, the precise route of the corridor has yet to be determined. Questions such as how goods will be transported, which Bangladeshi port will be used and how land and sea routes will be integrated remain under discussion. Several Bangladeshi diplomats who accompanied Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on his visit to China said the initial plan envisages an overland connection between Kunming and Kyaukphyu. From there, small feeder vessels would carry goods to Bangladesh across the Bay of Bengal. Tarique Rahman visited Beijing in late June. Earlier that month, then foreign secretary Asad Alam Siam had also visited the Chinese capital. Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman had travelled to Beijing in May. Chinese officials had outlined the initial concept of the proposed corridor during discussions with the two officials. . China's preliminary plan is to extend the land-based transport network from Kunming through Ruili, Muse and Mandalay in Myanmar to Kyaukphyu in Rakhine State. The connection between Kyaukphyu and Bangladesh would primarily be maritime. . The idea of establishing economic connectivity among Bangladesh, China and Myanmar is not entirely new. It has links to an earlier proposal for the Bangladesh-China-India-Myanmar (BCIM) Economic Corridor. members.title: "India has not formally set any conditions for returning Sheikh Hasina"
members.lead: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has said India has not imposed any formal conditions for returning ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who is currently staying in the country. However, Bangladesh will consider any formal conditions New Delhi may put forward on the matter. Shama made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday afternoon. On 12 November, a BBC Bangla report outlined two possible conditions India might seek in connection with Hasina's return to Bangladesh. The report claimed that officials in New Delhi had indicated two conditions for sending the ousted prime minister back to Bangladesh. According to the report, the first condition was that the Bangladesh Army would have to bring Hasina back, as she had travelled to India aboard a military aircraft belonging to the Bangladesh Army. . As for the second condition, quoting Indian foreign ministry officials, the report said the Bangladesh government would have to guarantee that Hasina would be given an opportunity to appeal against her death sentence and that her trial over allegations of crimes against humanity during the July massacre would be held afresh. . When asked about the BBC report during a regular briefing in New Delhi following its publication, Indian foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal declined to comment. Referring to former prime minister Sheikh Hasina as a convicted death-row prisoner currently staying abroad, Bangladesh's State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed said, "The Ministry of Law is examining how she will be brought back. We believe she will return under the extradition treaty, like any other accused person, and serve her sentence here. If India responds, it will make things easier for the people of Bangladesh and the government."
